_comment: Canonical machine-readable index of Carlos Duarte's backtested trading strategies. Single source of truth for (a) the Trading_Index AI hub (full ledger, including failures) and (b) the LTCMA website Backtests page (docs/backtests.html, generated by ~/LTCMA/scripts/24_backtests.py). The website renders ONLY entries with "public": true (curated showcase of what worked); failures stay in this file as internal institutional memory. To register a new strategy: append an object and re-run that script (or the LTCMA daily refresh). Verdict/metric values are pulled verbatim from each backtest's REPORT.md; where a metric was not computed it is the string 'n/a' (never guessed). badge: green=Deployable (survives the full protocol and beats the S&P on risk-adjusted terms), yellow=Ensemble component (real edge, not standalone-worthy), red=Pass/no edge (failed cost-adjusted tests).
protocol: Optuna smart-search -> walk-forward + purged CV -> Deflated Sharpe (DSR) + PBO -> Monte Carlo 100k-500k -> post-2024 held-out -> S&P 500 gate -> survival bar (max DD < 10%). Cost model: pessimistic retail (FxPro embedded per-bar spread + markup + stop slippage). Sizing: 1% fixed-fractional (R-multiple, sizing-invariant Sharpe).

strategies.name: Buy-the-Dip / Sell-the-Rip
strategies.what_it_tests: Daily-timeframe pullback-in-uptrend (systemic alpha): buy dips while price is above a long trend filter, optionally short rips in downtrends. Universe: SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM/EFA/EEM/EWW/GLD/SLV ETFs plus Gold/Silver spot, 2010-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: Robust but boring: 80-99% of the parameter space is positive-Calmar, so the edge is structural, not curve-fit. Deploy as a diversified SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble (DSR 0.60-0.80, PBO 0.37-0.48), not a single name. Lead with the caveat: it is a low-drawdown S&P-replacement (~2x the S&P's Calmar at ~1/8 the drawdown), NOT a return amplifier - at a 10% DD budget it earns ~10.1% CAGR vs a de-levered S&P's ~3.6%.

key_metrics.headline_config: SPY flagship (DSR 0.80); robust survivors that beat S&P Calmar: EFA, QQQ, SPY. maxDD/CAGR shown @1% risk.

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the SPY selected config (highest DSR alongside QQQ). maxDD -4.3% and CAGR 2.9% are at 1% fixed-fractional risk (in cash most days); scaled to a 10% DD budget the SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble earns ~10.1% CAGR. PBO range across instruments 0.37 (QQQ) to 0.85 (EWW). S&P full-window: CAGR 12.2%, maxDD -33.9%, Calmar 0.36.

strategies.name: Static SPY / IEF / GLD Diversification
strategies.what_it_tests: The deployable finding from the tactical-asset-allocation study: an equal-weight, low-turnover blend of US equity (SPY), 7-10y Treasuries (IEF) and gold (GLD), rebalanced monthly/quarterly, with an optional absolute-momentum cash filter. 2011-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: The momentum rotation didn't help - but the static equal-weight SPY/IEF/GLD blend beat every rotation variant tested: Sharpe 1.00, DSR 0.96, near-zero turnover, and it beats the S&P on Sharpe, Calmar and drawdown. Deploy as a low-cost diversified core (a 60/40-style -16.9% drawdown profile, not a sub-10%-DD product); the absolute-momentum filter is an optional crash overlay.

key_metrics.headline_config: Equal-weight SPY/IEF/GLD, monthly rebalance, turnover 0.35/yr; OOS (2025+) Sharpe 1.95

strategies.metrics_note: Highest-Sharpe, most timing-robust, lowest-turnover artifact in the entire TAA search (DSR 0.96 against ~1,200 effective trials). PBO 0.30 (full grid). MC maxDD 90% CI [-20.6%, -7.3%]. Benchmarks: SPY buy&hold CAGR 14.2%/Sharpe 0.87/maxDD -33.7%; 60/40 SPY/IEF CAGR 9.6%/Sharpe 0.98/maxDD -21.3%. The static blend beats SPY on Sharpe/Calmar/DD and ties 60/40.

strategies.name: Candle Range Theory (CRT) + Regime Filter
strategies.what_it_tests: ICT 3-candle range theory (C1 range -> C2 sweep+close-back-inside -> C3 reverse), gated by a daily 200-EMA trend filter on Gold. Tested vanilla and with regime overlays (trend alignment, ATR regime, day-of-week) on Gold, Silver, EURUSD, USDJPY. Span 2016 -> 2026-05-19.
strategies.verdict_line: CRT gated by a daily 200-EMA trend filter on Gold is a thin but real edge - PF 1.22, Sharpe 0.59, Calmar 0.33 - usable as one signal inside the regime-adaptive ensemble, never standalone. (Vanilla CRT, with no regime filter, had no post-cost edge - which is why this is an ensemble component, not a deployable system.)

key_metrics.headline_config: GOLD daily HTF, 3R target, + daily 200-EMA trend filter (507 trades, win 37%)

strategies.metrics_note: This report predates the full standing protocol: it used walk-forward IS (2016-2022) / OOS (2023-2026) but did NOT compute Deflated Sharpe or PBO, hence DSR/PBO = n/a.

strategies.name: Breedon & Ranaldo Local-Hours FX Rotation
strategies.what_it_tests: Published intraday FX pattern (SNB WP 2011-04): a currency tends to depreciate during its own country's trading hours and appreciate during foreign hours. Short/long each currency during its local session across EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, EURJPY, GBPJPY.
strategies.verdict_line: NOT DEPLOYABLE on any of the 5 pairs. The structural effect is real but tiny (EUR depreciates in Frankfurt morning) and smaller than realistic retail round-trip cost; every positive in-sample config fails DSR, held-out 2025+, Monte Carlo and the S&P gate. The intraday pattern appears largely decayed since its 2000s sample.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD EUR-short, Frankfurt 10:00, 4h hold, ATR x2.5, news-skip (best of 5 pairs; still fails)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the EURUSD leg (the only pair with positive full-period Sharpe); the other four are negative even in-sample. DSR 0.000 because raw SR 0.45 << noise-expected SR0 2.29 over 3000 trials. Held-out 2025+ Sharpe -0.45 (reverses). S&P bar: CAGR 11.91%, Sharpe 0.74, maxDD -33.92%.

strategies.name: Momentum Rotation TAA (rotation overlay)
strategies.what_it_tests: Antonacci/Faber-style tactical asset allocation: rank a pool of ETFs by trailing momentum, hold the top-N, with an absolute-momentum (trend) crash filter. Monthly/weekly/quarterly rebalance, 2011-2026. (The deployable byproduct - the static SPY/IEF/GLD blend - is catalogued separately as 'static_diversification'.)
strategies.verdict_line: PASS on rotation as standalone alpha. Relative momentum only helps in a broad pool with chronic laggards to avoid; in a tight good-diversifier pool it hurts. Nothing clears the <10% DD survival bar, and the best rotation's monthly headline is a month-end timing artifact (jitter blows DD to -36%). The only thing that survived deflation is plain diversification - see the 'static_diversification' entry.

key_metrics.headline_config: Pool A: 6m lookback, top-3/8, monthly, abs-mom filter (best genuine rotation; still fails survival bar + fragile)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are Pool A (best genuine rotation). DSR 0.91 is high only because the 216 grid configs are near-clones (mild deflation) - it means 'real positive-Sharpe portfolio', NOT 'rotation beats buy-and-hold'. PBO 0.30 full grid / 0.35 rotation subset. Run it weekly (not monthly) if deployed at all.

strategies.name: Cross-Asset Relative-Weakness (Buy-the-Laggard)
strategies.what_it_tests: Daily cross-sectional 'buy the day's laggard, bet it catches up' (optionally short the leader, dollar-neutral, corr-gated). Universes: SPY/QQQ, SPY/QQQ/IWM, SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA, XLK/XLF. The dollar-neutral pair test isolates the signal from market beta. 2010-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: PASS on all 4 universes - not real alpha. The honest test (dollar-neutral long-laggard / short-leader pair) makes ~0% CAGR and goes flat-to-negative out-of-sample; the 1-day laggard buy is outright negative (Sharpe -0.4 to -3.7). It's relative MOMENTUM, not reversal - the laggard keeps lagging. Long-only configs look positive only as diluted long-equity beta (still below SPY); DSR ~0, PBO 0.81-0.99 = definitively overfit.

key_metrics.headline_config: Isolated dollar-neutral pair, best of 4 universes (the honest test); long-only beta-proxy best Sharpe 0.74 but DSR 0.00 / PBO 0.91

strategies.metrics_note: best_raw_sharpe and CAGR are the isolated dollar-neutral PAIR (the clean test with market beta removed): pair full Sharpe 0.19-0.60, CAGR ~0%, OOS -0.44 to +0.69 (noise). DSR 0.00-0.17, PBO 0.81-0.99 across universes - definitively overfit. The only positive curves are long-only = diluted long-equity beta, all below SPY buy-and-hold (Sharpe 0.86, CAGR 14.2%).

strategies.name: Session-VWAP Mean Reversion (FX + Gold)
strategies.what_it_tests: Range-weighted session VWAP (Asia/London ET). 1H entry at Nsigma deviation (sweep 1.5-3.0), exit on revert-to-VWAP / Nsigma stop / 4H time-stop / session close. Long+short. EURUSD/USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD, FxPro M5 2014-present (Gold 2016+). FxPro M5 has no real volume so VWAP uses a high-low range proxy (documented approximation).
strategies.verdict_line: FAIL - DO NOT DEPLOY. A real but tiny GROSS reversion edge exists on EURUSD/GBPUSD/Gold (cost-off PF 1.46-1.62) but it is smaller than retail FX round-trip cost; best in-sample post-cost optimum is <1% CAGR on ~110-130 trades/decade. Deflated stats kill it: DSR ~0.00 every pair (the +1.6 in-sample Sharpes are pure selection from ~4-5k trials), PBO 0.52-0.93, walk-forward OOS-positive 0/17/67/0%. USDJPY net-negative even optimized; Gold held-out 2025 = -10.4 Sharpe. Same story as Breedon-Ranaldo.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD London short N=2.72sigma stop=3.96sigma: IS Sharpe +1.60 / PF 1.26 but DSR 0.00, PBO 0.84, WF 0% OOS+; 2025 held-out +5.63 Sharpe is a 22-trade noise sample. GBPUSD similar (IS +1.58, DSR 0.00, PBO 0.76).

strategies.metrics_note: best_raw_sharpe/CAGR/maxDD are EURUSD in-sample selected config; overfit (DSR 0.00). Gross-vs-net avg_R probe (cost off -> pessimistic on): EURUSD +0.122->+0.056, USDJPY +0.035->-0.050, GBPUSD +0.151->+0.071, GOLD +0.176->+0.005. S&P gate: SPX CAGR 13.4% Sharpe 0.79 - no config within an order of magnitude on any axis. VWAP weight = range proxy (no real volume in FxPro M5; TickVolume has a 10x 2018 feed break).

strategies.name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB) - FX + Gold
strategies.what_it_tests: Zarattini-style opening-range breakout adapted to FX/Gold session opens. Range = high/low of first N min (5/15/30/60) after London 03:00 / NY 09:30 / Tokyo 19:00 ET. Long above range high (symmetric short) only if the breakout N-min bar closes beyond the range AND body>=atr_body*ATR(5) AND body>=body_frac*range (false-break filter). Stop = opposite range edge; targets 1R/2R/3R/chandelier-trail. M5 intrabar fills, per-pair pessimistic spread+slippage. EURUSD/USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD, FxPro M5 2008-present.
strategies.verdict_line: FAIL - DO NOT DEPLOY. Across all 4 instruments the deflated stats are unanimous: DSR=0.00 (the 0.14-0.54 in-sample Sharpes are entirely explained by the ~8000-trial joint session/N/param search), PBO 0.79-0.93 (the in-sample-best config lands below the OOS median ~80-93% of CSCV splits = severe overfit), and annual-reoptimized walk-forward Sharpe is -0.44 to +0.24 (zero to negative real-money). The false-break ATR/body filter only shrinks trade counts to noise (196-308 trades / 16y on JPY/GBP/Gold = ~12-19/yr); when loosened (EURUSD N=5 short) you get 2954 trades but a -54.9% drawdown. Held-out 2025 incoherent: GBPUSD/Gold marginally + on 27-32 trades (noise), USDJPY -0.64, EURUSD -1.32. Same grave as Breedon-Ranaldo and VWAP-MR: any gross edge is below retail FX round-trip cost.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD london N=15 short trail: IS Sharpe 0.54 / CAGR 10.8% but MDD -54.9%, DSR 0.00, PBO 0.83, WF -0.44, held-out 2025 Sharpe -1.32. The 3 low-DD configs (USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD short, N=60) are 0.14-0.48 IS Sharpe on 196-308 trades = statistically thin, all DSR 0.00 / PBO 0.79-0.93.

strategies.metrics_note: best_raw_sharpe/CAGR/maxDD shown are EURUSD IS-best (highest IS Sharpe, catastrophic DD). Every selected config across instruments is a SHORT. S&P gate: SPX buy-hold IS 2008-2024 CAGR 8.6%/Sharpe 0.51, OOS 2025 CAGR 17.6%/Sharpe 1.02 - no ORB config beats it on any axis. MC 100k +50% cost halves-to-zeros the already-marginal CAGR. Engine: M5 fills, ATR(5) on N-min bars no-lookahead, Bucharest->ET tz-correct, pessimistic stop-before-target tie-break.

strategies.name: SMA Crossover - EURUSD (+ USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD)
strategies.what_it_tests: The retail-classic moving-average crossover, tested as the baseline sanity check after a practitioner called it his "most profitable bot." Fast SMA crosses ABOVE slow SMA -> long; crosses BELOW -> short. Crossover pairs 10/20, 20/50, 50/200; ATR-based stop (1.5-3.0x); exits 1R/2R/3R/chandelier-trail/opposite-cross. Entry next-bar-open (no look-ahead), M5 intrabar stop/target fills, per-pair pessimistic spread+slippage, 1% risk. Timeframes 1H (primary)/4H/1D. FxPro M5 2014-present resampled.
strategies.verdict_line: FAIL - DO NOT DEPLOY, unanimous across EURUSD/USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD. The 0.33-0.76 in-sample daily Sharpes are entirely a multiple-testing mirage: DSR ~ 0.00 on every instrument (per-obs sr_hat 0.02-0.05 sits BELOW sr0 0.07-0.10, the expected max under the null across the ~5,000-trial joint tf/pair/dir/exit/ATR search - i.e. random search would have beaten it). Annual-reoptimized walk-forward is incoherent (-1.31 EURUSD to +0.50 USDJPY) and the held-out 2025 sign flips OPPOSITE to walk-forward on every pair = regime luck, not edge. PBO 0.13-0.99 (EURUSD 0.99 = maximally overfit). The apparent winners are single-trend beta dressed up as strategy: USDJPY long-only (17.9% CAGR) just rides the 2021-24 yen-carry downtrend (held-out -0.37, MDD -33.5%); XAUUSD long-only rides gold (held-out +1.65 only because gold ripped in 2025, WF -0.30); EURUSD short-only is curve-fit to 2014-22 EUR weakness (every WF fold negative). Fast variants self-destruct on cost (1H 10/20 = PF 0.87, MDD -96%). No config beats S&P buy-hold (IS CAGR 11.2%/Sharpe 0.70) on any axis; the <10% MDD bar is blown on USDJPY (-33.5%) and XAUUSD (-24.2%). Same grave as ORB / Breedon-Ranaldo / VWAP-MR.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD (the specific claim): 4H 10/20 short 1R, IS Sharpe 0.33 / CAGR 2.3% / MDD -10.9% but DSR 0.001, PBO 0.99, WF Sharpe -1.31 (all 6 folds negative), held-out +1.53 on 51 trades (contradicts WF). USDJPY (highest CAGR): 1H 20/50 long opposite-cross, IS Sharpe 0.76 / CAGR 17.9% but MDD -33.5%, DSR 0.006, held-out -0.37 = the yen-carry trend, not a crossover edge.

strategies.metrics_note: best_raw_sharpe/CAGR shown are the highest-IS-Sharpe pair (USDJPY) whose headline is pure trend beta with -33.5% DD; EURUSD is the named "most profitable bot" claim and posts DSR 0.001 / PBO 0.99 / WF -1.31. S&P gate: SPX buy-hold IS 2014-2024 CAGR 11.2%/Sharpe 0.70/MDD -33.9%, OOS 2025 CAGR 17.6%/Sharpe 1.02 - no SMA config beats it on any axis. MC 100k: P(MDD<10%)=0.00 for USDJPY/XAUUSD; +50% cost barely moves the already-marginal CAGR (edge is direction not cost, because the survivors are long-hold trend rides). Engine: numba state-machine, SMA cross -> next-bar-open entry, M5 intrabar fills, pessimistic stop-before-target, reverses on opposite cross. Reusable for any continuous-HTF FX signal.

strategies.name: EMA Pullback-in-Trend (Multi-Timeframe)
strategies.what_it_tests: The boring-classic continuation setup: established trend = price vs 200-EMA; pullback to 20/50-EMA within last N bars; entry on confirmation candle (close-above-EMA / bullish-engulfing / inside-bar-break); ATR(14) stop; target 2R / 3R / structure (recent swing) / chandelier-trail; symmetric short. Sizing 1% fixed-fractional, R-multiple metrics. Universe: FX (EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY) + metals (XAUUSD/XAGUSD) at 1H/4H/1D from FxPro M5 (real per-bar broker spread + slippage), and US indices (SPY/QQQ/IWM/EFA/EWW) daily via yfinance (0.10% RT). 20 combos.
strategies.verdict_line: DO NOT DEPLOY. No combo clears the validation bar - zero reach 'deploy' or even 'ensemble component'. The setup has a REAL but thin structural edge on the daily timeframe (positive Calmar across 75-99% of the parameter space on XAU, SPY/QQQ/IWM/EFA/EWW dailies, and EUR/GBP/USDJPY dailies), but the single optimised parameter set is overfit everywhere: PBO >= 0.63 on every concept-positive combo. The least-bad tier ('promising / regime-dependent': XAUUSD_1D, IWM_1D, XAUUSD_4H, SPY_1D, EURUSD_1D) is concept-robust (fCal+ >= 0.80) and beats S&P on Calmar, but all fail PBO and lean on tiny (3-17 trade) held-out windows. XAUUSD_1D is the standout (DSR 0.68, fCal+ 0.94, held-out Sharpe +1.64) yet still fails PBO 0.77. Intraday is cost-destroyed: every 1H FX/silver combo is net-negative after the real FxPro spread (EURUSD/GBPUSD 1H Sharpe < 0, MaxDD -29% to -51%); 4H is marginal-to-negative. Nothing here beats the existing Buy-the-Dip ensemble - EMA-pullback is a noisier cousin of buy-the-dip-in-trend and loses that contest.

key_metrics.headline_config: XAUUSD_1D (the standout, still fails PBO): pullback_ema=20, confirm=engulfing, atr_mult=1.52, target=structure, pull_window=12, time_stop=16, swing_lb=13, long_only; IS Sharpe 0.99 / Calmar 0.87 / CAGR 3.2% / MaxDD -3.4% @1% risk; DSR 0.68, PBO 0.77, OOS Sharpe +1.64 (10 trades), WF +0.48. QQQ_1D has the highest DSR (0.90) but PBO 0.94 and OOS -0.19. metrics shown for XAUUSD_1D.

strategies.metrics_note: Protocol applied at protocol-compliant trial depth: Optuna 350 IS trials/combo + 4-fold annual walk-forward (80 trials, 10-day embargo) = ~13.4k total trials across 20 combos; DSR + PBO (CSCV, 16 blocks, top-80); Monte Carlo 100k (IID bootstrap + 50%-cost stress + +/-1-bar entry jitter); held-out 2025+ never touched in selection. All Sharpe/CAGR/MaxDD computed on a DAILY-RESAMPLED equity series so 1H/4H/1D and S&P are directly comparable. Engine: numba-JIT trade loop, next-bar-open entry, OHLC pessimistic fills (gap-through fills at open, stop wins ties with TP). 14/20 selected configs chose long_only - the symmetric short was optimised away on most. S&P gate: SPX buy-hold full-window CAGR 12.0% / Sharpe 0.73 / MDD -33.9% / Calmar 0.35; 12/20 combos beat S&P on Calmar (driven by tiny @1% risk DDs, not absolute return - all sub-4% CAGR). Reusable code: code/data.py + engine.py + optimize.py + run_all.py + montecarlo.py + stats.py (reuses buy_the_dip's DSR/PBO verbatim).

strategies.name: Intraday Momentum (Gao/Han/Li/Zhou JFE 2018) - first H1 -> last H1
strategies.what_it_tests: JFE 2018 hypothesis: sign of the first intraday-bar return predicts the last-bar direction of the same session. Documented on US equity ETFs. FX adaptation tested two session pairings (London-first -> NY-last; Tokyo-first -> London-last) on EURUSD/USDJPY/GBPUSD/XAUUSD M5 data 2014-present (FxPro, Europe/Bucharest -> UTC, local-tz session anchors). Stop = atr_k x ATR(20,H1); flat at the close anchor; 1% risk; pessimistic per-pair spread. Exhaustive 162-cell grid (first_win x last_win x threshold x atr_k x session).
strategies.verdict_line: NOT DEPLOYABLE on all 4 instruments. The JFE finding does NOT carry to FX. Three independent failure modes converge on FAIL: (1) gross sign-carry diagnostic shows hit-rates 48-51% across 72 (sym x session x window) cells with no Bonferroni-significant cell; (2) the effect is also dead in the original SPY/QQQ universe in the recent ~2yr 1h sample (hit ~49.5%, t<1) -- a published-anomaly decay story, not an FX-specific issue; (3) even where gross sign is positive (Gold tokyo_london, +1.2 bp/trade peak), the edge is smaller than the FX round-trip cost. Selected IS configs deflate to DSR ~ 0 across all instruments; walk-forward Sharpes -0.05 to -0.81; held-out 2025+ Sharpes -0.68 to -1.75.

key_metrics.headline_config: GBPUSD tokyo_london, first_win=120, last_win=30, threshold=0.002, atr_k=0.5. IS Sharpe 0.38 / DSR 0.00 / WF -0.20 / OOS 2025+ Sharpe -1.75 (n=18).

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics shown for the best IS instrument (GBPUSD); all 4 fail. DSR is essentially zero on all instruments (2.9e-36 EUR / 2.2e-35 GBP / 6.1e-26 JPY / 1.0e-7 XAU). PBO is misleadingly low (0.00-0.13) because the entire grid is noise-similar -- the IS-best is not differentiated from the rest. MC 100k baseline MDD p5 ranges -12.4% (USDJPY) to -52.3% (EURUSD) -- well below the <10%-DD survival bar. S&P 500 IS 2014-2024 CAGR 11.2% / Sharpe 0.70 / MDD -33.9%; OOS 2025+ CAGR 17.6% / Sharpe 1.02. No intraday-momentum config beats it on any axis.

strategies.name: Donchian 20/55 Breakout + TSMOM Filter (Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen)
strategies.what_it_tests: Donchian channel breakout (entry 10/20/30 prior-period high/low, exit 5/10/15) gated by Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen time-series momentum filter (30/60/120-bar sign), with Turtle-style pyramiding (1-4 units at +0.25/0.5/0.75 ATR(20) intervals), symmetric long/short, channel-low trailing stop, 1% risk per unit. H4 + 1D timeframes. Universe: EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, XAUUSD (FxPro M5 -> H4/1D), SPY + QQQ (yfinance daily). 2014-2026.
strategies.verdict: Ensemble component ONLY with HMM gold-trend regime gate; 23y Dukascopy revalidation (2026-05-28) confirms demotion and pushes toward standalone-fail
strategies.verdict_line: 23-YEAR DUKASCOPY REVALIDATION (2026-05-28): the 8y FxPro window was masking regime dependence. On 23y D1 Dukascopy XAUUSD with 0.05% RT cost: IS Sharpe collapses 0.71 -> 0.27 (prior-winner config) or 0.39 (Optuna best across 432-cell grid), IS Calmar 0.56 -> 0.09, IS MDD -3.9% -> -13.4%. PBO 0.55 (FAILS <0.5), WF Sharpe -0.08 over 10 annual folds (negative when re-fit honestly), MC P(DD<10%)=0.01 on best config. Cohort decomposition is the smoking gun: 2003-07 LOSES, 2008-12 wins during GFC gold rally (Sharpe 0.66), 2013-17 DEAD (Sharpe 0.02), 2018-22 marginal (0.40), 2023-26 rally bonanza (Sharpe 1.50). Edge exists only in secular gold rallies - 8y FxPro window captured one such rally and 70% of another, so it looked structural. It is not. Stay yellow ONLY as HMM-regime-gated component; without the gate this is red.

key_metrics.headline_config: Prior-winner config (XAUUSD 1D, entry_p=30, exit_p=5, tsmom_lb=120, pyramid_units=2, atr_interval=0.75) on 23y Dukascopy: IS Sharpe 0.27 / Calmar 0.09 / MDD -13.4%. Best Optuna config on 23y: e10/x5/k120/py4/a0.25 with IS Sharpe 0.39 / Calmar 0.245 / MDD -28.6%.

strategies.metrics_note: REVALIDATION METRICS shown above are from the 23y Dukascopy run (2026-05-28). Original 8y FxPro metrics (deprecated, regime-contaminated): IS Sharpe 0.76, Calmar 0.49, MDD -7.8%, DSR 0.83, PBO 0.45. The collapse from 8y to 23y is the 'gold-secular-trend' artifact: cohort decomposition shows the edge is essentially zero outside 2008-12 and 2023-26 rallies. S&P full-window 2003-2026: CAGR 9.5%, MDD -56.8%, Sharpe 0.58, Calmar 0.17.

strategies.name: Ensemble #14 — Regime-Aware Sleeve Allocator (Capstone)
strategies.what_it_tests: Regime-conditional monthly allocation across 4 ungated sleeves (Buy-the-dip ensemble · Static SPY/IEF/GLD · CRT regime-Gold · Donchian-XAU with gold-trending filter). SARS_regime label drives portfolio weights (drift/calm/stress/crisis). One hard kill-switch on influence_hmm_state==2 AND HY_OAS_z>1.5. Architectural capstone of the 2026 backtest campaign.
strategies.verdict_line: DEMOTED 2026-05-31 after real-sleeve GFC analog test on extended 21y sample 2005-2026. GFC monthly MaxDD -13.59% / daily -17.16% -- FAILS 10% bar by 359/716 bps. Full 21y Sharpe 1.04, MAR 0.39 (criterion 14 ❌). Architectural reason (Finding #9): real BTD has SMA150 internal trend filter making it the SAFEST sleeve in GFC (DD -4.95%, 321/569 days flat); gating moves weight FROM BTD (50%→0%) INTO Static SPY/IEF/GLD (DD -21%) at the worst possible time, actively HURTING by 5.5pp daily / 3.7pp monthly DD vs ungated. Static drift-weight 50/30/20 (no gating) PASSES the same GFC bar at -9.85% monthly with 15 bps headroom. Use that instead.
strategies.failure_reason: External regime-gated portfolio weighting is architecturally inverted when one sleeve has internal regime detection. Generalizes Finding #1 (signal-level double-gating) to portfolio-weighting level.

strategies.metrics_note: Architecture works. The simpler static 50/30/20 drift-weight version (no regime gating at all) is strictly better on Sharpe (1.33) AND MaxDD (-3.92%). The regime gating earns its keep in stress (Sharpe edge +0.68) and crisis (+0.80) but loses in drift (-0.18). Donchian-XAU contributes 0.17%/yr - drop it. Kill switch fires 0/194 mo (HY_OAS history too short to validate <0.5% claim).

strategies.name: Static Drift-Weight Sleeve 50/30/20 (BTD / Static SPY-IEF-GLD / CRT-Gold) — GFC-tested
strategies.public_carve_out: PBO_structural 0.325 is above the strict 0.30 bar. Carlos has approved a carve-out for ensembles of correlated sleeves (candidate set is mechanically correlated by construction). 11/12 survival criteria pass cleanly; the 12th is borderline-fail on the strict reading and passes on the soft reading.
strategies.what_it_tests: Fixed 50/30/20 allocation across Buy-the-dip ensemble (SPY+QQQ+EFA) / Static SPY-IEF-GLD blend / CRT regime-Gold daily 3R, monthly rebalance, no regime gating, no kill switch. Packaged as a standalone backtest after Ensemble #14 revealed this simpler version strictly dominates the gated capstone on Sharpe and MaxDD. Vindicated 2026-05-31 by the real-sleeves 21y extended GFC analog test (passed 10% bar at -9.85% monthly with 15 bps headroom).
strategies.verdict: Deployable — GFC-tested (cleaner than the now-demoted Ensemble #14)
strategies.verdict_line: Sharpe 1.33, MaxDD -3.92%, CAGR 5.06% over 194 months (16.2y, post-2010). Extended 21y test (2005-2026) including real 2008 GFC: GFC monthly MaxDD -9.85% PASSES 10% bar with 15 bps headroom; -9.81% daily with M5-vol-matched CRT-Gold passes both. Strictly dominates Ensemble #14 (which fails the same GFC test at -13.59% monthly) on risk-adjusted return AND drawdown AND PBO tightness AND Monte Carlo robustness AND GFC survival. Beats SPY on Sharpe (1.33 vs 1.00) and Axis B (2.83x leverage matches SPY CAGR at -11.1% DD vs SPY -23.9% DD). Held-out 2025+ Sharpe 1.95. Cost-shock +50% only drops Sharpe to 1.28. 5/5 walk-forward folds same-sign with min OS Sharpe 1.01. Deploy on time horizon >= 5 years for the compounding effect to matter.

gfc_metrics.note: Passes 10% monthly bar in all 3 CRT-Gold sensitivity scenarios (daily proxy / scaled / zeroed); passes daily bar in 2 of 3. Vindicates against the prior 'no 2008 GFC in sample' caveat from 2026-05-30. Architectural lesson (Finding #9): the strategy wins by NOT gating — real BTD's internal SMA150 trend filter does the defending in stress (BTD GFC sleeve MDD only -4.95%; flat 321/569 GFC days). Ensemble #14's gating moves weight away from this defense and gets punished.

strategies.metrics_note: 11 of 12 survival criteria pass cleanly. The 12th, PBO < 0.30, is borderline-fail at 0.325 structural / 0.476 perturbation; same correlated-candidate-set caveat as Ensemble #14 (which had PBO 0.40). This strategy's PBO is TIGHTER than the gated capstone's. Caveats logged in REPORT: (1) no 2008 GFC in sample - real GFC analog could push MaxDD to 6-10%; (2) CRT-Gold covers only 63% of months in the early sample - the 20% sleeve sat at 0% for 71 of 194 months; (3) beats SPY on Sharpe and Axis B but NOT on raw CAGR (5% vs 14%) - this is a sleep-better-at-night risk-reduction product, not an alpha amplifier; (4) OOS 2025+ Sharpe 1.95 partly rides gold and SPY ripping, not pure strategy alpha.

gold_dependence_check.verdict: C: Returns are genuinely consistent. Gold does NOT save the strategy.
gold_dependence_check.test: Built four counterfactual variants and compared: v0 baseline (with gold), vA (no GLD in Static), vB (drop CRT-Gold), vC (no gold anywhere).
gold_dependence_check.headline: Strip all gold from the strategy: CAGR drops 3bps to 5.03%, Sharpe falls 8bps to 1.25, MaxDD widens from -3.92% to -8.69% but still clears the 10% survival bar, beta to GLD drops from 0.13 to 0.04.
gold_dependence_check.interpretation: Gold provides risk insurance (5pp of MaxDD), not return. Strategy generates positive Sharpe in every cohort including the 2013-18 gold-bear stretch (Sharpe 0.89). Removing gold actually IMPROVES gold-bear performance (Sharpe 0.71 -> 1.09) because gold drags during bears. The Donchian-XAU 'secular gold rally artifact' pattern (Finding #2 in STRATEGY_LOG) does NOT apply here.
gold_dependence_check.implication_for_deployment: Keep public verdict (green). Frame the card as 'diversified across equity+bonds+gold' rather than gold-centric. Implied GLD-equivalent exposure is only 12.1% of the portfolio. Most of the risk is equity-like (BTD + Static SPY/IEF).
gold_dependence_check.remaining_concern: vC (no gold) at -8.69% MaxDD in 2010-26 would likely breach 10% in a 2008-GFC simulation. The Static SPY/IEF sleeve without GLD had no offset in 2008. v0 (with gold) is more comfortable for the 2008 stress test.

strategies.verdict: Architectural conclusion: gating HARMS when sleeves have internal regime detection
strategies.verdict_line: Ensemble #14 (gated) GFC monthly MaxDD -13.59% / daily -17.16% — FAILS 10% bar by 359/716 bps. Static drift-weight 50/30/20 (ungated) PASSES at -9.85% monthly with 15 bps headroom; -9.81% daily with M5-matched CRT-Gold. Architectural reason: real BTD with SMA150 filter is the SAFEST sleeve in GFC (DD -4.95%, 321/569 days flat as cash); gating moves weight FROM BTD (50%→0%) INTO Static SPY/IEF/GLD (DD -21%) at the worst possible time. Gating actively hurts by 5.5pp daily / 3.7pp monthly DD vs ungated. Finding #9 added to STRATEGY_LOG: external regime-gated weighting harms when sleeves have internal regime detection (generalizes Finding #1 from signal to portfolio level).
